rows.note: Use 原因 as the all-purpose noun for what produces an event or result.

example.english: The cause of this accident still hasn't been found.
example.traditional: 呢次意外嘅原因仲未搵到。
example.jyutping: ni1 ci3 ji3 ngoi6 ge3 jyun4 jan1 zung6 mei6 wan2 dou2

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose way to say that someone or something makes a result happen.

example.english: Continuous rain can cause the venue to get completely wet.
example.traditional: 連續落雨令到場地濕晒。
example.jyutping: lin4 zuk6 lok6 jyu5 ling6 dou3 coeng4 dei6 sap1 saai3

rows.note: Use this colloquial choice when emphasizing the resulting situation, especially an unwanted one.

example.english: That mistake can cause me to lose sleep all night.
example.traditional: 呢個錯誤搞到我成晚瞓唔着。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 co3 ng6 gaau2 dou3 ngo5 seng4 maan5 fan3 m4 zoek6

rows.note: Use this when something triggers an event, reaction, or other occurrence rather than making a person do something.

example.english: This news can cause widespread panic.
example.traditional: 呢個消息引起大家恐慌。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 siu1 sik1 jan5 hei2 daai6 gaa1 hung2 fong1

rows.note: Use 理由 for a justification or sufficient reason, including a reason for taking or avoiding an action.

example.english: I have sufficient cause not to go.
example.jyutping: ngo5 jau5 cung1 fan6 lei5 jau4 m4 heoi3

rows.note: Use this for the forceful or coercive slice of cause to do, when someone is made to act against their will.

example.english: Their threats can cause me to apologize immediately.
example.traditional: 佢哋啲威脅逼我即刻道歉。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 di1 wai1 hip3 bik1 ngo5 zik1 hak1 dou6 hip3
